title: [drawer] Drive swipe gestures natively to stop per-frame re-rasterization

labels.name: component: drawer
labels.description: Changes related to the drawer component.

body: Fixes #4863 ### Problem While a Drawer was open, every swipe `touchmove` re-rasterized the sheet's content instead of staying compositor-only. The `touchmove` bubbled into React's delegated touch system, and processing it there made Chrome invalidate and repaint the document and full-screen popup once per move (~2 paints per move). The translate was already a cheap composited transform — the repaints came from the event-dispatch path. ### Fix Drive the swipe from a native, capture-phase `touchmove` listener. Once the Drawer claims the gesture it calls `stopPropagation()` so the move never reaches React's delegated handlers, forwarding it via a typed `moveFromNativeTouch` hook method. Propagation is preserved for cases the Drawer must not hijack (native scroll, range inputs, pinch-zoom, text selection). `getDragTransform` also moves to `translate3d`. No consumer CSS or workarounds required. ### Results [Heavy drawer stress benchmark](https://mui-2026-drawer-performance.netlify.app/) (800-node payload, includes Vaul), headless Chromium, 20× CPU slowdown, paired same-session runs, medians: | Lib | Total busy | Paint | Paint ev | Avg move task | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Base UI (before) | 981 ms | 341 ms | 78 | 17.1 ms | | Base UI (after) | 631 ms | 70 ms | 6 | 8.9 ms | | Material UI | 723 ms | 328 ms | 79 | 14.4 ms | | Silk | 586 ms | 80 ms | 0 | 4.2 ms | | Vaul | 1121 ms | 86 ms | 6 | 10.2 ms | Base UI before → after: paint 341 → 70 ms (−79%), paint events 78 → 6, avg move task 17.1 → 8.9 ms (−48%), total busy −36%. The per-move content re-rasterization is gone; paint no longer scales with the heavy content. Notes: numbers reflect main-thread work during the gesture. `Total busy` = all main-thread time in the swipe window; `Avg move task` = per-move input-handler latency — not comparable across libraries (Silk travels via native scroll, so it offloads the drag to the compositor and delivers fewer JS moves). Material UI's `SwipeableDrawer` keeps an 800-node paper mounted while closed, which inflates absolute numbers for every row equally, so treat cross-library absolutes loosely; the Base UI before/after delta is unaffected. ## Before ## After ### Changes - Handle swipe moves in a native capture-phase `touchmove` listener and call `stopPropagation()` so they don't reach React's delegated handler. Native scroll, range inputs, pinch-zoom, and text selection still propagate. - Add `moveFromNativeTouch` to `useSwipeDismiss` so the native listener feeds the gesture without a synthetic React event. - Switch the swipe transform to `translate3d`.
